title: Rat learning experiments as evidence for morphic resonance
place_text: London, New York, San Francisco, Melbourne, Beijing

tellings.quote: now there's actual evidence from a long series of experience with rats that that actually happens

plain: Once rats in one place learn a task, rats elsewhere learn it faster, and the scientist Rupert Sheldrake says a long series of experiments with rats shows this happens, in cities from London and New York to San Francisco, Melbourne and Beijing. He tells Michels that this is "actual evidence" for what he calls morphic resonance, his idea that what members of a species learn makes it easier for others of that species to learn the same thing, even far away. He does not name the studies.
